To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
capture fisheries and aqua-culture are both sustainable and unethical, but aquaculture is more sustainable than capture fisheries.
the ethics of capture fisheries and the sustainability of aquaculture are influenced by the interactions between human institutions and social groups.
the ethics and sustainability performance of capture fisheries and the two major aquaculture systems are highly variable.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the ethics of the social, economic, and political processes that influence the wellbeing, autonomy (freedom), and fairness of different interest groups involved in the production, consumption, and governance of seafood.
the ethical and sustainable management of fisheries and aquacultural systems.
the ethics and sustainability implications of the seafood industry, and the role of human institutions and social practices in shaping its future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in general, the ethical and sustainable performance of capture fisheries and, especially, aquaculture systems is highly variable and depends on their specific social, economic, and ecological context.
, in general, large-scale capture fisheries and aqua-culture are less sustainable and more unethical than small-scale fisheries and aquacultures.
both capture fisheries and aquiculture are sustainable, but only if they are well governed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ethical and sustainable production of seafood is dependent on the ability of human institutions to manage the social, ecological, and economic interactions between fisheries and aquacultural systems, and their surrounding social and ecological contexts.
capture fisheries and aquiculture are not intrinsically ethical or sustainable.
capture fisheries are more sustainable, but aquaculture is more ethical.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ethical and sustainability challenges faced by capture fisheries and aqua­culture are complex, interlinked, and require integrated solutions.
capture fisheries and aquiculture systems can be designed and managed to be ethical, equitable, and sustainable.
the ethics and sustainability performance of capture fisheries and aquatic farming are not necessarily mutually exclusive.
